description: Calls an LLM using a named prompt from PGC_Prompt. Resolves template variables from local_state into the prompt. Also injects PGC_SystemContext rows where inject_for includes the prompt intent_category. Runs the 2-attempt validation/correction loop. Writes the validated output object to output_key.

input_contract.description: intent_category key into PGC_Prompt — identifies which prompt to use
local_state key where the validated LLM output object is written

Additional keys in input (beyond prompt) become {{key}} substitution variables in the prompt text. Key name must match the placeholder exactly — snake_case user_input matches {{user_input}}, NOT {{userInput}}. user_input is also sent as the LLM's human/user message.
Routing token — defaults to "next"
Routing token — use "cancel" for unrecoverable failures
snake_case slug for a domain-specific prompt not yet in PGC_Prompt. Must equal input.prompt. design_workflow_prompts reads this to classify the step as reuse/create/convert.

Full prompt text for a new domain-specific prompt, with {{template}} variables. Consumed by design_workflow_prompts to insert a new PGC_Prompt row. Required when prompt_category is present and the prompt does not yet exist.
Model alias for the new prompt: 'cheap' or 'smart'. Stored verbatim in PGC_Prompt.model; llm-harness.mjs resolves to the actual model ID at runtime via llm_model_aliases.
JSON Schema for the expected LLM output. Stored in PGC_Prompt.output_schema and used by the step-executor validation loop.

output_contract.description: The validated LLM output object written to local_state[output_key]

description: Runs a pure synchronous JS IIFE expression via acorn AST gate + vm.runInNewContext(200ms timeout). Two sandbox bindings: (1) items — the resolved value of input_key from local_state. (2) local_state — the full workflow state object; use local_state.key_name to read any prior step output. Expression must return the output value. No async, no I/O, no Node globals. Use for data transforms, score tallies, filter operations, loop state mutations, boolean flag computation. IMPORTANT: PostgreSQL numeric, decimal, and money columns are returned as strings by the DB driver — always wrap in parseFloat() or Number() before arithmetic (e.g. parseFloat(local_state.row.price) * qty). Skipping this turns + into string concatenation and silently produces wrong values.

input_contract.description: Synchronous JS IIFE. items = resolved input_key value. local_state = full workflow state. Must return output value. Example: "(function(){ return items.map(function(t){ return Object.assign({}, t, { domain: local_state.proposed_scaffold.domain }); }); })()"
Optional dot-path into local_state resolving to the input value bound as 'items'. Omit when the expression reads everything it needs directly from local_state.
Dot-path where the result is written to local_state. Comma-separate multiple keys (e.g. "a,b,c") to destructure an object return value into multiple top-level local_state keys simultaneously.
Routing token — supports step:N for backward loops

output_contract.description: Result of the expression written to local_state[output_key]

description: Suspends workflow execution and presents a dialog to the user. Execution resumes when the user clicks an option button. Gate types: confirm (read message, click button — output_key written when context_key also present), form (collect any number of typed values — the ONLY gate that captures user input; output_key receives an object of every field), list_selection (review a table of records and pick one), review_object (review key-value summary), choice (single-select with lettered buttons A/B/C, per-option description lines — output_key written with selected value; when a choice option carries a modal descriptor, the typed modal text is written to the option's own output_key if declared, or to the step-level output_key if not), followup_prompt (shows a message with an "Ask follow-up" button that opens a free-text modal — no output_key written by the gate itself; the follow-up text is handled by the EXP tier). Each option has its own on_select routing token. special_buttons appear as action buttons only — never in description lists — and support modal descriptors for overlay text input. Optional reveal field: add { button_label, content } to any gate_type to toggle content visibility within the same gate — content supports standard markdown formatting. Optional reveals field: array version of reveal — one reveal panel per entry (e.g. one per table). Each entry is { button_label, content }. Supports an inline array or a {{template}} reference to a local_state array.

input_contract.description: confirm | form | list_selection | review_object | choice | followup_prompt. (text_input is DEPRECATED — it still runs for workflows built before form existed, but must never appear in a new one; use a form with a `textarea` field for free-form prose.) form: collects any number of typed values in ONE gate — declare them in `fields` (each { name, type }, where type is text | textarea | select | multi_select | radio | checkbox | date | time | datetime, naming WHAT is collected, never a widget). output_key receives a single object keyed by field name. Options for select/multi_select/radio/checkbox come from `options` (fixed) or `options_key` (a local_state dot-path, so a dropdown can offer rows the workflow already queried). Never collect a date or an enumerable value as free text and then parse it with an llm_call — use a typed field. A picker is deterministic, parsing prose is not. Common pattern for choice: pair with reveal field for 'question → reveal answer → grade response' workflows where hidden content must be verified before the user can accurately select an option. list_selection: every context_key item ({id, fields?, secondaryAction?} — fields is a plain object of column name -> value, pre-formatted in a preceding js_transform, not here; no forced Name/Title synthesis, the record's own field names/values pass through as-is) renders as one row in a single markdown table (one column per distinct field key across every item, sparse where an item lacks a given key), plus one shared selection control and one Select button (label/style from item_action, label defaults to 'Select') applied uniformly unless an item already carries its own secondaryAction. The selection control is a dropdown of every selectable row — grouped by source table when a level spans more than one, so ids colliding across tables stay unambiguous — falling back to a plain id text box past Slack's 100-option cap. The user picks a row and clicks Select: the selected row is written to output_key and the gate routes via item_action.on_select, which is required and is resolved directly, never via a matching options[] entry (that would render a redundant duplicate button) — e.g. drill-down into a back-edge step that fetches/displays that one record. What selecting means is the calling workflow's concern, expressed through on_select's target, never through a different gate_type.
Message shown to user — supports {{template}} substitution

Dot-path into local_state for the data shown in the dialog. Required for list_selection and review_object. Optional for confirm — when present, the selected action value is written to output_key. Not used by form (form declares its inputs in `fields`; a dropdown's choices come from a field's own options_key).

form gates only, and required for them. One entry per value to collect: { name, type, label?, optional?, placeholder?, options?, options_key?, option_value_key?, option_label_key? }. `type` is one of text | textarea | select | multi_select | radio | checkbox | date | time | datetime and states WHAT is collected — never a Slack widget name. select/radio yield one value; multi_select/checkbox yield an array. radio/checkbox cap at 10 options, select/multi_select at 100. CEILING: one gate presents roughly 40 fields before it exceeds what a single message can hold, and it does not degrade past that — it fails to render at all. The count is fields per row multiplied by rows, so a data-driven form fits ~40 rows at one field each but only ~13 at three.

Array of option objects — must include at least one with action/value: "cancel" in either options or special_buttons. Shape varies by gate_type: confirm/list_selection/review_object use { label, action, on_select }; choice uses { value, label, description, on_select } where value is the machine identifier written to output_key, label is the short button text (e.g. "A", "B"), and description is the explanatory sentence displayed above the buttons. Any option may carry a modal descriptor: { title, input_label, placeholder, multiline } — clicking the button opens an overlay modal; the typed value is written to the option's own output_key if declared, otherwise to the step-level output_key on submit. Any option in a choice gate may carry iterator: '<local_state_key>' — at runtime buildDialog expands it into one button per item in localState[iterator], resolving label/value/description tokens against each item. Use instead of a preceding js_transform when buttons come from a variable-length array. Only one option per gate should carry iterator; include a separate Cancel option without it. `action` and `on_select` are different things and are never interchangeable: `action` is a display/behaviour label the renderer groups on (confirm | cancel | save | done | rate | …), while `on_select` is the routing token deciding where the run goes next. `on_select` accepts "next" (follow the step's on_success), "end", "cancel", or a step key naming a step that exists — bare ("4") and prefixed ("step:4") are both accepted and identical after normalisation. An action name is never a valid on_select value.

Optional array of action buttons that appear after options buttons but are never rendered in description_list or content fields. Same shape as options per gate_type. Use for Cancel, Other, or modal-trigger buttons that should not appear in the displayed option list. Supports modal descriptor: { title, input_label, placeholder, multiline } — clicking opens an overlay modal; typed value is written to output_key on submit, overriding the button value. The cancel obligation can be satisfied here instead of in options.

Legacy text_input gates only — do not use in new workflows (a form field carries its own `label`). Short label shown above the inline text input. Defaults to "Your input". Keep concise (2-5 words). The full instructions go in message_template.

For form: local_state key receiving ONE object of every collected field, keyed by field name (e.g. { period: "2026-07-01", category_id: "3" }). For confirm with context_key: local_state key where the selected action value is written. For choice: local_state key where the selected option.value is written — when the option carries a modal descriptor, the modal typed text (inputValue) is written instead of the button value.

Optional. local_state key recording WHICH option the user clicked (an option's `value` on choice gates, its `action` on all others). Set it when a LATER step must know the gate's outcome. The case that needs it: a save-and-continue loop, where 'Save' and 'Done' both run the SAME write and diverge only AFTER it — the decision has to survive the write so a condition can read it downstream. Routing the two buttons to separate chains instead would duplicate the write. When you set action_key, every option must carry a DISTINCT action ('save', 'done', 'cancel'): two buttons both using the conventional 'confirm' are indistinguishable to everything downstream. Independent of output_key — a form gate uses BOTH, because output_key holds the FIELD VALUES, not the button.

static | dynamic — what the choice set IS, never how it should be drawn. `static` means the options were written out at design time: the count is a property of the design, and a workflow run repeatedly is answered fastest when every value is visible at once (a fixed rating scale). `dynamic` means the set is computed at runtime and may hold three entries or three hundred, and may grow over time. Describes the choice set only — a Cancel or other control button alongside a dynamic option set does not make the set static. The engine reads this off the step when the field is absent: options given as a {{template}} reference, or an option carrying `iterator`, are dynamic, because that is the only way a set gets built at runtime; anything else is static. Declare it only to override that reading. Which widget carries the set, and what limits apply, belong to the experience layer; a workflow never names a widget.

Routing when user clicks a cancel option — REQUIRED on every human_gate. Must point to a valid step_label or "cancel". Both the cancel option (action/value: "cancel" in options or special_buttons) AND this on_cancel routing field are mandatory — satisfying one without the other fails L1 validation.
Default routing when no on_select override applies
Routing on gate execution error — not user cancellation

Optional progressive disclosure for decision-making — toggles content visibility within the same gate. Use when the user needs to view hidden information before making their choice: e.g. 'attempt → verify → decide' patterns where visible content is processed first, hidden context is revealed, and an option is selected in the same interaction moment. Do NOT use (use separate steps instead) when: the reveal action itself produces data (timestamps, logs, computations) needed downstream; different routing logic applies before vs after the reveal; or the revealed content requires an external or LLM call. Composable with any gate_type. Shape: { button_label: string, content: string | array }. content supports {{template}} substitution. A string or array of strings renders via basic mrkdwn formatting (bold, italic, links) — NOT markdown table syntax, which the underlying block cannot render. An array of plain record objects (e.g. [{title, count}, ...], no syntax/verb/command field) automatically renders as a real Slack table, one column per distinct key across the array — do not hand-format pipe-delimited text to fake a table. Both button_label and content must be non-empty. Use reveals (array) instead when the number of panels is determined at runtime. A reveal is display only: it carries no on_select, does not route, and does not advance the run. Never pair one with a matching option (a "Show Answer" button alongside a reveal produces two controls for one action).

Array version of reveal — renders one reveal panel per entry (e.g. one per table). Each entry is { button_label: string, content: string | array }; same content rendering rules as reveal (basic mrkdwn for strings, automatic Slack table for an array of plain record objects). Supports an inline JSON array or a {{template}} reference to a local_state array of {button_label, content} objects. Use instead of reveal when the number of panels is determined at runtime.

description: Creates a physical PostgreSQL table via SERV-Schema createTable. Also registers the table in PGC_Schema and PGC_TableMap. Used inside iterators driven by a tables array from an LLM call.

input_contract.description: Full table definition object — tableName, target, columns, foreignKeys, constraints, triggers. May be "{{item}}" inside an iterator.
Routing token

description: Inserts one row or a batch of rows into any PGC or PGD table. Table must be registered in PGC_TableMap with allow_insert: true. Single row: returns the inserted row including generated id. Array: calls addRows and returns all inserted rows.

input_contract.description: Table name — must be registered in PGC_TableMap

Row object or array of row objects. System columns (id, created_at, updated_at) are populated automatically. When an array is supplied the step calls addRows in a single request — no iterator needed. Supports {{template}} — a template resolving to an object or array is passed directly.
local_state key where the inserted row object is written
Routing token
Routing token

output_contract.description: The inserted row including populated id

description: Reads rows from a PGC or PGD table with optional filters, ordering, and limit. Writes the rows array to output_key. Empty result (no matching rows) is not an error — returns an empty array.

input_contract.description: Table name — must be registered in PGC_TableMap
Array of { column, op, value } filter objects. Ops: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, like, in, is_null, not_null, jsonb_contains
{ column, direction } — direction is "asc" or "desc"
Maximum number of rows to return
local_state key where the rows array is written
Routing token
Routing token

output_contract.description: Array of row objects written directly to local_state[output_key]. NOT wrapped in a {rows:[...]} envelope. Use {{output_key.length}} to count results, never {{output_key.rows.length}}.

description: Updates rows in a PGC or PGD table matching the given filters. Filters must be non-empty — unfiltered mass updates are rejected. Returns updatedCount and updated rows.

input_contract.description: Table name — must be registered in PGC_TableMap with allow_update: true
Non-empty array of { column, op, value } filter objects — must scope to specific rows. Ops: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, like, in, is_null, not_null, jsonb_contains
Object of column → new value pairs
local_state key where { tableName, updatedCount, rows } is written
Routing token
Routing token

description: Deletes rows from a PGC or PGD table matching the given filters. Filters must be non-empty — unfiltered mass deletes are rejected. Best practice: precede with serv_query + human_gate confirm so the user confirms which records are deleted.

input_contract.description: Table name — must be registered in PGC_TableMap with allow_delete: true
Non-empty array of { column, op, value } filter objects — must scope to specific rows. Ops: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, like, in, is_null, not_null, jsonb_contains
Routing token
Routing token

description: Inserts or updates each row in rows depending on whether an existing row matches all matchColumns values. Use this instead of a serv_query lookup + js_transform diff + conditional serv_insert/serv_update chain whenever a batch of records needs to be inserted if new or updated if already present (e.g. importing budget data, syncing recurring records). Workaround upsert — no table currently declares a compound unique constraint on matchColumns, so matching is query-then-write (LIMIT 1 on the first row satisfying matchColumns), not a native INSERT ... ON CONFLICT.

input_contract.description: Table name — must be registered in PGC_TableMap with allow_insert: true AND allow_update: true
Non-empty array of column names whose combined values identify an existing row — e.g. ["year", "month", "category_id"]. Must be a flat array of strings, never per-row filter objects.
Non-empty array of full row objects to upsert — one per record
local_state key where { tableName, inserted, updated } is written
Routing token
Routing token

description: Lists assembled entities via SERV-Entity listEntities. Returns root columns plus jsonb_agg child arrays. Use instead of serv_query for domains with child tables (e.g. recipes with ingredients and steps).

input_contract.description: Entity name matching PGC_EntitySchema.entity_name — e.g. "Recipe"
Array of { column, op, value } filter objects. Ops: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, like, in, is_null, not_null, jsonb_contains applied to the root table
Maximum number of entities to return
local_state key where the entities array is written
Routing token
Routing token

output_contract.description: Array of assembled entity objects — root columns plus child arrays keyed by aggregation outputKey

description: Fetches one assembled entity by id via SERV-Entity getEntity. Returns root columns plus child arrays. Use for id-based single-record lookup.

input_contract.description: Entity name matching PGC_EntitySchema.entity_name — e.g. "Recipe"
Primary key id of the root entity row
local_state key where the assembled entity object is written
Routing token
Routing token

output_contract.description: Assembled entity object — root columns plus child arrays. Single object, not an array.

description: Loads a full entity schema by reading PGC_EntitySchema for join topology and PGC_Schema for live column definitions. Returns entity_name, root { table, columns }, and children [{ table, alias, fk_column, output_key, columns }]. System and FK columns excluded. Use before llm_call steps that need the schema to parse or validate entity input.

input_contract.description: Entity name matching PGC_EntitySchema.entity_name — e.g. "Recipe". Supports {{template}} substitution.
local_state key where the full schema object is written
Routing token
Routing token

output_contract.description: { entity_name, description, root: { table, columns: [{name,type}] }, children: [{ table, alias, fk_column, output_key, columns: [{name,type}] }] }

description: Inserts a multi-level entity into its PGD tables in topological order. Derives parent-child relationships from the entity schema (output of serv_entity_schema). Handles n-level hierarchies by threading FK IDs between levels (index-based matching) and self-referential tables via two-pass insert+update. Use after parse_entity_input has produced a parsed_entity.

input_contract.description: Full entity schema object from serv_entity_schema output ({{full_entity_schema}}). Must contain root.table and children array with parent/fk_column fields.
Parsed entity object from parse_entity_input llm_call ({{parsed_entity}}). Must contain root: {} and children: { <outputKey>: [...] }.
local_state key where the result is written
Routing token
Routing token

output_contract.description: { root_id: number, root_record: object, inserted_counts: { <alias>: number } }

description: Evaluates a template expression against local_state and routes to one of two named steps without performing any I/O or writing to local_state. Truthy: non-empty string, non-zero number, non-null object. Falsy: empty string, "null", "undefined", "0", "false". on_success and on_else are bare step keys (e.g. "2", "3a") — same rule as all other routing fields.

input_contract.description: {{template}} expression resolved against local_state — e.g. "{{quiz_done}}". Must resolve to a scalar truthy/falsy value. For complex conditions, pre-compute a boolean flag in a prior js_transform.
Step key to jump to when expression is truthy (e.g. "2", "3a"). A bare key and the "step:2" form are both accepted and identical after normalisation. Same format as all other routing fields.
Step key to jump to when expression is falsy (e.g. "3", "4b"). A bare key and the "step:3" form are both accepted and identical after normalisation. Same format as all other routing fields.

description: Dry-runs a workflow step array through three validation levels without calling real services. Level 1: static analysis — routing values, dead targets, missing templates, gate structure. Level 2: path execution using mock_outputs and simulation_paths decision scripts. Level 3: skip-path analysis (advisory). Used by create_workflow to validate generated steps before registration.

input_contract.description: Dot-path into local_state resolving to the steps array to simulate

Dot-path to the routing skeleton the step array was translated from. When present, Level 1 also checks that translation emitted exactly one step per design item and invented none of its own (skeleton_drift). The step set is locked once the skeleton is validated — only the design stage may add a step.
Dot-path to mock_outputs object — required for Level 2. If absent, runs Level 1 only.
Dot-path to simulation_paths array — required for Level 2. If absent, runs Level 1 only.

How far validation runs — 0 shape only, 1 adds static analysis, 2 (default) adds the routing matrix and data-flow trace. Level 0 answers whether each element is a step of the type it claims to be, with every field its contract marks required, which is the question a content-free routing sketch can answer. The retired boolean `input.skeleton` is still accepted and means level 0.
local_state key where the SimulateWorkflowResponse object is written
Routing token — taken when all levels pass
Routing token — taken when any level fails. Typically "step:N" to route back to a review gate.

output_contract.description: SimulateWorkflowResponse — { passed, paths_run, paths_passed, paths_failed, static_analysis, path_results, skip_path_warnings }

description: Sends a message to the user via the callback channel. The message_template is resolved against local_state. Does not block — fire and forget. No on_else field — errors are silently discarded. Typically the second-to-last step before end.

input_contract.description: Message text — supports {{template}} substitution from local_state
SQS message type — defaults to HUMAN_NOTIFICATION
Routing token — typically "end" on the final notify step. Only next and end are valid.

Optional collapsible panel attached below the message content — e.g. a large child-record list on an entity display notify. Shape: { button_label: string, content: string | array }. content supports {{template}} substitution. A string or array of strings renders via basic mrkdwn formatting (bold, italic, links) — NOT markdown table syntax, which the underlying block cannot render. An array of plain record objects (e.g. [{title, count}, ...], no syntax/verb/command field) automatically renders as a real Slack table, one column per distinct key — do not hand-format pipe-delimited text to fake a table. Use reveals (array) instead when the number of panels is determined at runtime.

Array version of reveal — renders one panel per entry. Each entry is { button_label: string, content: string | array }; same content rendering rules as reveal (basic mrkdwn for strings, automatic Slack table for an array of plain record objects). Supports an inline JSON array or a {{template}} reference to a local_state array of {button_label, content} objects.

description: Executes a single item_step once per element of an array in local_state. Always sequential — one item at a time. Collects results into output_key array after all items complete. execution_mode must always be "sequential". The item_step runs with the parent frame local_state plus the injected item binding.

input_contract.description: Dot-path into local_state resolving to the array to iterate over

Step definition executed once per item. Use {{item}} or {{item.field}} to reference the current element. All parent local_state keys are also readable. Two categories: non-suspending item_steps (serv_schema, serv_insert, serv_update, serv_delete, serv_query, llm_call, js_transform) run inline within a single Lambda invocation. Suspending item_steps (human_gate with gate_type: "choice") suspend the iterator after each item and resume on user response — only gate_type: "choice" is valid inside an iterator. Dynamic options pattern: set "options": "{{item.options}}" on the human_gate item_step — the single-token template resolves to the current item’s options array at runtime, enabling per-item dynamic choice lists built by a prior js_transform step.
Must always be "sequential". Omitting this causes non-sequential execution that exhausts Lambda concurrency on large batches.
local_state key in the PARENT frame where the collected results array is written after all items complete
Routing token after all items complete — defaults to "next"
Routing token if an item_step fails

output_contract.description: Array of outputValue from each item_step execution, written to the parent frame after all items complete

description: Terminal step — marks the workflow run as completed. No input or output fields. No routing fields. Every workflow must have exactly one end step and it must be the last step in the array.

Persists a memory record to PGC_Memory. content_key points to a local_state key containing a plain-text string. scope values support {{template}} substitution. token_estimate is computed automatically as Math.ceil(content.length / 4). Must be the last step after notify. Never fails the workflow run — errors are logged and execution continues.

input_contract.description: episodic | semantic | procedural
JSONB scope object — values support {{template}} substitution. e.g. {"domain": "{{input.domain}}"}
local_state key containing the plain-text content string to persist
Array of string tags for filtering. e.g. ["schema", "design_decision"]
Integer priority — lower = higher priority. Default 5.
Name of the workflow writing this memory (for attribution)
Step key inside the workflow (for attribution)
Routing token — typically "end". Defaults to "end".

If true, sets expires_at = now() on all existing PGC_Memory rows with matching scope and tags before writing the new row. Use for singleton memories (e.g. schema snapshots) that should replace prior versions.
